chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Mithami, from Aban ibn 'Uthman, from Ibn Abi Ya'fur, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

A man came to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله and said: “O Messenger of Allah, I asked a man by the Face of Allah, and he struck me with five lashes.” So the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله struck him with five more and said: “Ask by your own ignoble face.”

key_terms.اللَّئِيمِ: ignoble; a term of rebuke used in the Prophet’s statement
key_terms.النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِ: the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله, the one to whom the complaint was brought
key_terms.بِوَجْهِ اللَّهِ: by the Face of Allah; an invocation of divine sanctity in making a request
key_terms.خَمْسَةَ أَسْوَاطٍ: five lashes; the punishment mentioned in the report

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about asking people by the Face of Allah?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates an incident in which a man complained to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله after being struck for asking another man by the Face of Allah. The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله added five more lashes and rebuked him, indicating condemnation of using the divine name or sanctity in an improper or base manner. The report carries ethical and legal significance regarding reverence for Allah and improper forms of asking.
